header:
Date: 2026-06-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jamie Chen (Redwood SE), Olivia Brooks (Redwood CSM); Lena Ortiz (CISO), Marcus Hale (VP Eng), Ravi Kapoor (Lead SRE), Ana Morales (SecOps)
Recording: yes
Notes: pen-test closure, patch cadence, KMS/encryption, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, SDLC alignment
summary: High level: Vela just completed a third-party pen test; Redwood and Vela walked through findings, risk classification, and a pragmatic 30/60/90 patching playbook. Key topics included KMS/HSM integration for model keys, audit log retention and format, RBAC scoping for Dedicated/Private deployments, and secure SDLC adjustments. Action items focus on sharing redacted artifacts, mapping owners to fixes, and validating SSO/RBAC in a sandbox. There were a few transcription glitches on product names (Redwood Dedicaed mentioned) and minor crosstalk during Q/A.
topics: Pen test findings and CVSS triage
Patching cadence (30/60/90) and emergency patch windows
KMS/HSM integration and key rotation policy
RBAC/SSO (Okta/SAML) scoping for Dedicated and Private
Audit logs: retention, formats, and export for audits
Secure SDLC changes: dependency scanning, pre-commit hooks, and staging canaries
transcript:
[00:00] Samir (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run through the pen test wrap and the proposed patching playbook. Roughly an hour.
[00:16] Lena - CISO: Thanks, Samir. We want to confirm timelines for critical items and KMS mux, uh integration patterns.
[00:34] Jamie (SE): Yep, we'll surface the redacted findings first, then a mapping to remediation owners. Quick note, the pen test flagged a couple of things around token exposure in logs and an S3 bucket misconfig, and a couple of dependency CVEs.
[00:55] Marcus - VP Eng: When you say token exposure, is that internal KV cache keys, or API keys in application logs?
[01:12] Jamie (SE): Looks like API keys getting logged by a legacy worker in staging, and also some noisy traces where we leak partial tokens in stack traces. We'll attach exact lines in the redacted CSV.
[01:34] Lena - CISO: Our policy is immediate for critical - 72 hours? or do we want 24 for ir? we need to sync on SLA.
[01:50] Samir (AE): Redwood recommends 72 for critical by default but we can support emergency hotfix if you use Dedicated or Private with our ops support add-on. There was a note in the report about misconfigured IAM roles on the monitoring account.
[02:10] Ravi - Lead SRE: We run a weekly patch window on Tuesdays. Critical outside window goes through emergency change but that means some approvals. How does Redwood help speed this?
[02:30] Olivia (CSM): We can offer a runbook and an on-call triage play for the pilot period, and Jamie can document the fix steps.
[02:44] Jamie (SE): For the patching playbook: we proposed a 30/60/90 cadence. 30-day sprint to address critical and high with mitigation steps; 60 days to fully remediate medium; 90 days for low and backlog. Also suggested a hotpatch path for CVSS 9/10.
[03:05] Marcus - VP Eng: That fits with internal SLAs. Re: KMS, we need clarification on Redwood's KMS flows: are model encryption keys customer-managed?
[03:25] Samir (AE): Yes you can use your KMS - it's supported in Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption and a customer-managed KMS option for enterprise. Note: HSM-backed key wraps are available but require onboarding.
[03:45] Lena - CISO: Are key rotations automatic? what's the rotation window?
[04:00] Jamie (SE): Rotation is policy-driven; standard is 90 days but you can configure more frequent rotation. We do zero-downtime rotation via double-wrapping and a primary/secondary key provisioning pattern. There was a brief transcript misread as "double-wrap ping" earlier in our docs, so ignore that.
[04:20] Ravi - Lead SRE: How do audit logs look? We need structured, queryable events for access to keys, model invocations, and config changes, and exportable to Splunk/ELK.
[04:40] Jamie (SE): Audit logs include request-level metadata (route, model version, token id hashed), admin actions, rollouts, and key events. They ship in JSON with a stable schema and we can forward to your SIEM via syslog or cloud-forwarder. Retention configurable, 90 days default, up to and beyond for enterprise.
[05:05] Ana - SecOps: For compliance, we need immutable logs for a year and signature verification. Do you support WORM-style or append-only with signing?
[05:25] Samir (AE): We support append-only audit streams and can integrate with an external immutable store. Signature verification support via HMAC/SHA on the event payload is on the roadmap — we can provide attestations for Dedicated/Private today.
[05:45] Lena - CISO: There's also ISO-27001 gaps we flagged in the report (control docs around third-party monitoring). Any quick wins?
[06:02] Jamie (SE): Quick wins: update the inventory for third-party services, lock down S3 buckets with block public access, and adjust log redaction rules to mask tokens. We'll provide playbook snippets.
[06:20] [00:06:20] Speaker 1: sorry fuzzy audio — could you repeat the SSO bit?
[06:30] Samir (AE): Sure. On SSO: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and OIDC; we have an Okta guide and a G-Suite guide. For RBAC, we recommend least privilege roles mapped to Okta groups and we can do role templates for Admin/Operator/Viewer.
[06:52] Lena - CISO: Do templates cover pipeline/service accounts?
[07:05] Jamie (SE): Yes, includes service account patterns; we advise rotating service creds, storing in your KMS, and not using long-lived API keys. There's a small mis-transcription in the doc where "service account" became "surface account" but it's the same concept.
[07:26] Marcus - VP Eng: About private deployments: is network ingress restricted to our VPC via peering? We need data residency controls too.
[07:45] Samir (AE): Yes — Private deployments can be deployed in your VPC, with peering or on-prem options. Data never leaves your VPC unless you opt into telemetry. For Hosted we have region pinning and data residency features for EU/NA/APAC.
[08:05] Ravi - Lead SRE: Pen test called out a few dependency chain issues — npm packages with known CVEs. What's Redwood's recommended SDLC adjustment?
[08:24] Jamie (SE): Add dependency scanning in CI (Snyk or OSS scan), block merges until fixes for high/critical, add pre-commit hooks for secrets scanning, and include a staging canary with live traffic fraction to validate patches. We'll share sample pipelines.
[08:46] Lena - CISO: For the 30-day window, will Redwood commit resources to help remediate or is it documentation only?
[09:02] Samir (AE): For Dedicated/Private customers on an enterprise plan we can offer remediation support as part of a paid engagement — pair-programming with your SRE for up to X days. For Hosted customers we provide the playbook and runbook plus office hours.
[09:20] Ana - SecOps: The vuln report includes a medium issue labeled "unexpected admin endpoint" — can you walk through that?
[09:34] Jamie (SE): That one is path traversal in an internal admin UI that was exposed to staging. The fix is to enforce auth middleware and add a blocklist on the endpoint, and then rotate keys used by that service. We will mark it critical if exploitability is shown.
[09:56] Marcus - VP Eng: On logging of tokens — we need deterministic redaction. Is there a redact list we can push upstream?
[10:12] Jamie (SE): Yes, we have a redaction regex pack and options to send sanitized logs. We'll include those regexes in the playbook.
[10:30] [00:10:30] Lena - CISO: One item: KMS access audit — we need per-operator key use logs. Are those present?
[10:44] Jamie (SE): Key-use events are logged; we include principal, action, key id, and timestamp. For Private we can forward those to your audit cluster. For Hosted we store them and can export on request; retention depends on tier.
[11:05] Ravi - Lead SRE: Do you support HSM-backed keys with BYOK (bring your own key) in cloud KMS? We want HSM-level guarantees.
[11:22] Samir (AE): We support BYOK and HSM-backed keys via cloud KMS integrations or dedicated HSM for Private customers. There's extra onboarding and an attestation step.
[11:42] Marcus - VP Eng: About patch windows, our ops team prefers a weekend window for disruptive fixes. Will Redwood's hotpatch recommend canary deploys?
[11:58] Jamie (SE): Yes canaries, traffic shaping, and rollback playbooks are part of the remediation plan. We'll show example configs for continuous deployment using your existing CI.
[12:20] Ana - SecOps: Do you have metrics on mean time to remediation when customers accept the playbook?
[12:34] Olivia (CSM): We do internal medians: criticals usually remediated in 5-7 days with our managed ops; high in 21-30 days. We'll share anonymized benchmarks.
[12:50] [00:12:50] Speaker 2: audio drop for a sec, back now.
[13:05] Samir (AE): Next, on compliance artifacts: we'll provide a checklist mapping pen-test findings to SOC2/ISO controls and suggested evidence for auditors.
[13:24] Lena - CISO: We need that mapping. Also for ISO, the risk register needs entries for each finding.
[13:36] Jamie (SE): Agreed; we'll include a risk register template and suggested narrative per finding.
[13:50] Marcus - VP Eng: A practical question: how do rollbacks interact with key rotation? If we rotate keys and then rollback code, are there compatibility issues?
[14:08] Jamie (SE): That's why we recommend double-key strategy; on rollback the previous key remains valid for decrypting existing objects until TTL expires. We'll document edge cases.
[14:28] Ravi - Lead SRE: On exportability, can we get a CSV of vuln findings with lines linking to git commits?
[14:42] Jamie (SE): Yes the pen-test deliverable includes CSV and we've cross-referenced PRs for our internal fixes where possible. We'll attach that.
[15:00] [00:15:00] Lena - CISO: Regarding SSO, we plan to roll out Okta groups. Do you support SCIM for group sync?
[15:15] Samir (AE): SCIM provisioning is supported for enterprise tiers and Private. For Hosted we support SAML group mapping.
[15:30] Marcus - VP Eng: Any breaking changes to RBAC when we onboard? We need a migration plan.
[15:44] Jamie (SE): Migrations are staged: create role templates, apply read-only mode for a week, then flip. We'll provide step-by-step and rollback steps.
[16:05] Ana - SecOps: The pen-test suggested improving secrets handling in CI — caching creds in runner. Suggestions?
[16:20] Jamie (SE): Use ephemeral tokens in CI, store long-lived secrets in your KMS with short-lived service tokens; rotate and limit scope. We'll include GitLab/GitHub Actions examples.
[16:38] Lena - CISO: Will the fix for the S3 misconfig be documented in the playbook as a checklist?
[16:50] Olivia (CSM): Yes, the bucket hardening checklist will be front and center: block public access, restrict IAM, enable default encryption, and attach lifecycle rules.
[17:05] Samir (AE): Quick pause — any blockers to the proposed cadence?
[17:14] Marcus - VP Eng: Approvals for emergency change are the only blocker. We need delegated approval to the on-call SRE for hotpatches.
[17:26] Lena - CISO: We can create a scoped approval policy for hotfixes to reduce bureaucratic delay.
[17:36] Jamie (SE): We'll include a template approval workflow and suggested approval TTL.
[17:48] [00:17:48] Ravi - Lead SRE: For the 30-day sprint, can Redwood provide patch scripts for the vuln fixes?
[18:03] Jamie (SE): Yes, for the top 10 items we'll provide patch scripts or remediation CLI steps where feasible.
[18:20] Ana - SecOps: On the audit log export format, do you include geo/ip of requests?
[18:32] Jamie (SE): Yes, we include requester IP, region, user agent, and route metadata, but IPs can be hashed on request.
[18:46] Marcus - VP Eng: About data residency: if we use EU-only region, are backups replicated outside EU?
[18:58] Samir (AE): For Private and Dedicated you control replication. Hosted has region pinning options and daily backup location control for enterprise. We'll show the policy matrix.
[19:14] Lena - CISO: A nit: the pen-test report had a couple of false positives in our environment; can you help triage?
[19:26] Jamie (SE): Sure we'll help triage and mark false positives in the shared CSV.
[19:38] [00:19:38] Speaker 3: small crosstalk, sorry.
[19:46] Jamie (SE): On CI changes, consider adding an automatic release gating integration with the vuln tracker: block on high/critical.
[19:58] Marcus - VP Eng: We'll add that to our backlog if you provide the PR template.
[20:10] Samir (AE): Final bit: we'll produce three artifacts this week — redacted pen-test PDF, CSV with issue IDs, and the patching playbook with checklists and RBAC templates.
[20:26] Lena - CISO: Good. Also we want the KMS key usage logs forwarded to our Splunk instance — what's the next step?
[20:36] Jamie (SE): We'll set up a forwarding test to your sandbox SIEM; Olivia will coordinate credentials and the test timeline.
[20:48] Olivia (CSM): I'll send calendar invites for the SIEM test and the 30-min follow-up.
[21:02] Ravi - Lead SRE: Are there any recommended monitoring alerts for rolling out fixes?
[21:12] Jamie (SE): Yes: high error rates, spike in request latency, unexpected auth failures, and audit log volume spikes. We'll include alert templates (PagerDuty bindings).
[21:30] [00:21:30] Lena - CISO: One last compliance ask: can Redwood provide an SOC2 controls mapping doc for these findings?
[21:44] Samir (AE): Yes we'll include a SOC2 and ISO mapping in the artifact pack.
[21:56] Marcus - VP Eng: Ok thanks, that helps.
[22:08] Ana - SecOps: Quick question: will patch testing include model regression checks? We don't want inference quality regressions when we patch runtimes.
[22:22] Jamie (SE): Good call — include a small eval harness as part of pre-release canary testing. We'll share a minimal prompt test-suite for the models you're using.
[22:38] Samir (AE): Alright, recap next steps and owners.
[22:44] [00:22:44] Olivia (CSM): Recap: Jamie to upload redacted pen-test and CSV by Tue; Olivia to schedule SIEM forward test and follow-up meet; Ravi to share patch calendar and CI details; Lena to confirm hotpatch approval policy.
[23:05] Lena - CISO: Thanks everyone.
[23:12] Samir (AE): Thanks, we'll follow up in writing.
[23:20] [end of recorded portion — remaining minutes used for off-the-record chats and scheduling logistics that were not transcribed cleanly — some audio dropouts and overlapping talk toward the end]
